questions.text: Which of the following are NOT insured by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)?

options.text: All commercial banks including branches of foreign banks functioning in India
All State, Central and Primary cooperative banks
Local area banks and Regional rural banks
All of the Above are insured by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC).

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Primary cooperative societies.

Key Points

  • Primary cooperative societies are NOT insured by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC).
    • Commercial Banks: All commercial banks including branches of foreign banks functioning in India, local area banks, and regional rural banks are insured by the DICGC.
    • Cooperative Banks: At present all cooperative banks are covered by the DICGC.​

    • Primary cooperative societies are not insured by the DICGC.

questions.text: Deposit Insurance corporation act was formed in _____ year and came into force in _____ year.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 1961,1962.

  • The Deposit Insurance Corporation (DIC) Bill was introduced in the Parliament on August 21, 1961. After it was passed by the Parliament, the Bill got the assent of the President on December 7, 1961, and the Deposit Insurance Act, 1961 came into force on January 1, 1962. 
  • The Government of India, in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India, introduced a Credit Guarantee Scheme 1960. The Reserve Bank of India was entrusted with the administration of the Scheme, as an agent of the Central Government, under Section 17 (11 A)(a) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and was designated as the Credit Guarantee Organization (CGO) for guaranteeing the advances granted by banks and other Credit Institutions to small scale industries.
  • The Reserve Bank of India also promoted a public limited company on January 14, 1971, named the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. (CGCI).
  • With a view to integrating the functions of deposit insurance and credit guarantee, the above two organizations (DIC & CGCI) were merged and the present Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) came into existence on July 15, 1978.
  • DICGC insured the money deposited by the customers in the commercial and co-operative banks up to the 5 lakh rupees.
  • DICGC headquarters is in Mumbai and its chairman is RBI deputy governor.
  • Currently (Aug-2020) Dr. M.D. Patra is the chairman of DICGC.

About RBI​

  • RBI was established on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act,1934.
  • Current Governor of RBI is  Sanjay Malhotra
  • Sir Osborne Smith was the first governor of RBI and C.D Deshmukh was the first Indian governor of RBI.
  • It operates the currency and credit system of the country.
  • It is called the Bankers Bank of India.
  • It formulates, implements, and monitors the monetary policy.

questions.text: In October 2025, in a major move to strengthen the Indian banking system, a comprehensive set of sectoral reforms was announced, including risk-based deposit insurance premiums and the adoption of an Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model. It also updated the Basel III norms effective April 2027. Which regulatory body is responsible for implementing these reforms?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is RBI.

In News

  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) announced major banking sector reforms in 2025, including risk-based deposit insurance premiums, adoption of the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) model, and updated Basel III norms.

Key Points

  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed four key measures to modernize and strengthen India’s banking system.
  • The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) will now charge risk-based premiums based on each bank’s risk profile instead of a uniform 12 paise per ₹100 deposit.
  • The new Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework replaces the incurred loss model, requiring banks to provide upfront for estimated credit losses.
  • This approach enhances credit quality evaluation using borrower risk, repayment history, and macroeconomic indicators.
  • Revised Basel III capital adequacy norms effective April 2027 provide differentiated risk weights for MSMEs and home loans to sustain growth.
  • The reforms aim to strengthen prudential regulation, capital adequacy, and financial stability within Indian banking.
  • Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Payments Banks (PBs), and Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) are temporarily exempted from the new capital framework.

Additional Information

  • DICGC covers deposit insurance for all commercial and cooperative banks in India up to ₹5 lakh per depositor.
  • Basel III norms are international standards developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) to strengthen bank capital.
  • The RBI regulates monetary policy, financial institutions, and credit systems across India.
  • The ECL model aligns domestic banking standards with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS 9).
  • Improved lending discipline and early recognition of stressed assets will reduce future systemic risks.
  • RBI
    • Established in - 1935
    • HQ - Mumbai
    • Governor - Sanjay Malhotra

questions.text: Deposit insurance contributes to confidence in the banking system by protecting small depositors against loss in case of bank failure, up to prescribed limits. The broader purpose of such protection is to:

options.text: remove all incentives for prudential regulation
allow unrestricted and undocumented cross-border movement without security verification
reduce panic and support confidence in formal banking
substitute for all forms of supervision by the central bank
guarantee profitability of all banking institutions

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is reduce panic and support confidence in formal banking.

Key Points

  • Deposit Insurance is a mechanism designed to protect depositors, particularly small depositors, from losing their money in the event of a bank failure.
  • The primary objective of deposit insurance is to enhance public confidence in the banking system. It ensures that even if a bank fails, depositors will recover their funds up to a prescribed limit.
  • This system reduces the likelihood of panic among depositors, as people are assured that their money is protected. Hence, the statement is correct.
  • Deposit insurance contributes to financial stability by preventing mass withdrawals or "bank runs," which can destabilize banks and the broader economy.
  • The broader purpose of deposit insurance is not only to protect depositors but also to encourage trust in formal banking systems, reducing reliance on informal or unregulated financial channels. Hence, the correct answer is: reduce panic and support confidence in formal banking.

Additional Information

  • Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC):
    • In India, deposit insurance is provided by the DICGC, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
    • The DICGC insures deposits up to ₹5,00,000 per depositor per bank, including principal and interest. This limit was revised in 2020, from the earlier limit of ₹1,00,000.
  • Benefits of Deposit Insurance:
    • It protects small and retail depositors who may not have the resources to assess a bank's financial health.
    • It fosters trust in the banking sector, encouraging people to save and deposit their money in formal financial institutions.
    • Deposit insurance also facilitates financial inclusion, as people in rural and semi-urban areas are more likely to use formal banking services when they feel secure about their deposits.
  • Limitations of Deposit Insurance:
    • The insurance coverage is limited, and amounts exceeding the insured limit are not protected.
    • It may create a moral hazard, as depositors and banks might take on excessive risks, assuming that losses will be covered.
    • Deposit insurance is not a substitute for prudential regulation and supervision by central banks or regulatory authorities.

Important Points

  • Misinterpretations of Deposit Insurance:
    • Option 1: “Remove all incentives for prudential regulation” is incorrect because deposit insurance does not eliminate the need for proper regulation and supervision of banks.
    • Option 2: “Allow unrestricted and undocumented cross-border movement without security verification” is incorrect because deposit insurance has no role in cross-border financial transactions.
    • Option 4: “Substitute for all forms of supervision by the central bank” is incorrect, as deposit insurance complements, not replaces, central bank oversight.
    • Option 5: “Guarantee profitability of all banking institutions” is incorrect because deposit insurance protects depositors, not banks or their profitability.
  • Global Examples of Deposit Insurance:
    • In the United States, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) provides deposit insurance up to $250,000 per depositor per bank.
    • In the European Union, deposit insurance schemes offer protection of up to €100,000 per depositor per bank.

questions.text: The Reserve Bank of India increased the Insurance cover on bank deposits from Rs 1 lakh effective from February 4, 2020. Which among the following is the new insurance cover on bank deposits?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e. Rs 5 lakh.

  • The Reserve Bank of India increased the Insurance cover on bank deposits from Rs 1 lakh effective from February 4, 2020. 
  • The new insurance cover on bank deposits is ​Rs 5 lakh.
  • The decision has been taken with a view to giving protection to depositors.
  • The cover is given by the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the RBI.
  • Banks would be paying a premium of 12 paise against 10 paise per Rs 100 deposit.
  • Please note that DICGC ensures all commercial banks including branches of foreign banks functioning in India, local area banks and regional rural banks also. The insurance cover had remained Rs 1 lakh since 1993.

questions.text: Which of the following is not insured under DICGC?
questions.explanation:
• DICGC stands for Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation and is a subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
  • It provides insurance to all the banks registered under the guidelines of the RBI Act 1934.
  • It provides insurance against all the deposits such as savings, current, fixed, recurring, etc. However, deposits which are not covered are deposits of the foreign governments, deposits of the central or the state governments, deposits of the state land development banks with the state co-operative banks, various inter-bank deposits, any amount due on account of and deposit received outside India and any amount, which has been specifically exempted by the corporation with the previous approval of RBI.
  • The banks need to pay the premium for the insurance amount. 
  • Each of the depositor, who has an account in a bank, is insured up to a maximum of Rs 1 lakh for both principal and interest amount held by them as on the date of cancellation or liquidation of bank’s license or the date on which the scheme of amalgamation/merger/reconstruction takes place.
  • DICGC chairman-B.P.Kanungo (Deputy Governor of RBI)
  • DICGC HQ-Mumbai

The correct answer is Guarantee.

Key Points

  • DICGC stands for Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation.
  • All deposits in commercial and cooperative banks, both domestic and international are insured by DICGC except for deposits by the government both domestic and foreign.
  • Primary cooperative societies are not insured by the DICGC.
  • DICGC insures a maximum of Rupees Five Lakh for each depositor which includes both principal and interest

questions.text: What is the name of the online tool launched by DICGC for depositors to track their claim status?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Daava Soochak.

In News

  • The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) has launched an online tool “Daava Soochak” for depositors to track their claim status.

Key Points

  • Depositors can use the Daava Soochak tool to track the status of their claims for banks placed under All Inclusive Directions (AID) post-April 1, 2024.
  • The DICGC’s primary role is to reimburse insured amounts to depositors of failed banks.
  • The deposit insurance coverage limit has been enhanced to Rs 5,00,000 per depositor as of February 4, 2020.

Additional Information

  • Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC)
    • Headquarters: Mumbai, Maharashtra.
    • Chairman: M.D. Patra.

questions.text: Asset Reconstruction company is associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Asset Reconstruction companies are those which come at the essence of non – performing assets of commercial banks. these companies are registered under the securitization and Reconstruction of financial assets and enforcement of securing interest (SARFAESI) Act, 2002. It is regulated by Reserve Bank of India as a NBFC. Its functions include Acquision of financial assets, change / takeover of management. Rescheduling of debts and settlement of drives payable.

questions.text: DICGC is responsible for giving insurance to deposits, insurance of how much amount is given by DICGC to NBFC?

options.text: No insurance is provided to NBFC

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option (5) i.e. No insurance is provided to NBFC.

  • DICGC stands for Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation and NBFC stands for Non-Banking Financial Company.
  • NBFC provides loan and advances facilities.
  • DICGC is a wholly subsidiary of the RBI it was established in 1978.
  • It was established under the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation Act, 1961.
  • DICGC earlier provided insurance to all the depositors of insured bank up to 1 lakh rupees but from February 2020 the amount has been increased from 1 lakh to 5 lakhs.
  • DICGC does not provide insurance to NBFC.
